title: gh-909 AgentGateway v0 execution
description:
## Background
Issue #909 establishes one placement-independent `AgentGateway` v0 contract and one canonical `createAgentHost()` construction path. It replaces divergent Agent assembly in Agent, Workspace, Core, CLI, playground, and delegation consumers while preserving the existing browser wire, transcript layout, authorization boundaries, plugin ownership, and runtime behavior.

## v0 scope
This epic closes only when G1, AH0, MIG-WS, MIG-CORE, MIG-CLI, MIG-PG, and MIG-DEL are complete. V0 is honest Level B: bounded event replay, process-lifetime request idempotency and effect admission, scope-bound keyset pagination, an in-process derived activity index, and deterministic no-journal rename. Durable event offsets, a durable request ledger, durable activity checkpoints, immutable snapshot pagination, recursive remote-wire validation, catalog revival, package qualification, plugin trust cleanup, and remote-host hardening remain follow-up work.

## H0/A0 dispatch gate and ready-state protocol
Graph creation is not owner approval. Before H0, this epic stays labeled `ready-for-human`, G1 stays `deferred`, and every other implementation bead stays blocked by dependencies. No child may move to `in_progress`.

At H0 the owner must approve both this plan and the #905 amendment that makes v2 a versioned additive extension of the v0 semantic core. Record the dated approval and authoritative amendment reference in this epic's notes with `br update wt-391-forward-0jpy --notes "<dated owner approval and amendment reference>"`. Then and only then run `br update wt-391-forward-0jpy.1 --status open`. Do not undefer any other bead; they remain dependency-blocked.

## Execution and branch protocol
Execute one implementation bead per worktree, branch, and pull request. Create each worktree under `.worktrees/issue-909-<bead-suffix>` from the canonical checkout and use branch `issue-909/<bead-id>`. A bead moves to `in_progress` only after every blocker is closed and the executor has claimed that bead. Keep each pull request in progress until merged.

Before owner review or merge, post a proof-of-work comment for the current pull-request head SHA. It must list changed paths, every exact automated command and result, exact manual or E2E steps and observations, rollback instructions, and any waiver or known gap. Close the bead only after merge and after the proof comment refers to the merged head.

## Dependency shape
G1 freezes the shared contract and reusable conformance suite. AH0 depends on G1 and builds the sole Host factory plus embedded Gateway. MIG-WS, MIG-CORE, MIG-CLI, MIG-PG, MIG-DEL, durable streaming core, and catalog revival depend on AH0. The five v0 migration lanes may run in parallel after AH0. Follow-up dependencies encode only genuine implementation prerequisites; follow-up completion never gates this v0 epic.

## Global v0 invariants
Shared code has no `node:*` imports or `Buffer`. App-issued scopes are provenance checked and bind current membership plus the complete Workspace/storage partition. Host identity, provider mechanics, roots, credentials, and live objects never enter v0 transport DTOs. One native session has one writer. Compatible Agents share one canonical Environment lease; incompatible placement or provisioning fails closed. Legacy routes, NDJSON framing, browser errors, prompt behavior, and all three transcript-layout branches remain byte-compatible.

## Graph and metadata proof
Before dispatch and after graph edits run `br dep cycles`, `bv --robot-insights`, `br lint`, and `br ready --json`. Expected pre-H0 result: no cycles, no lint failures, this epic is blocked by open children, G1 is deferred, and no issue-909 implementation child is ready.

## Considerations
Do not back-propagate follow-up requirements into v0. Do not remove compatibility wrappers, routes, symbols, exports, or files without the applicable recorded owner contraction approval. Do not rename `BORING_AGENT_HOST_ID` without a separately approved compatibility migration. No deletion, destructive Git operation, force push, or direct push to `main` is authorized.

## Success Criteria
The canonical closure criteria are in this bead's acceptance-criteria field and are mandatory.
acceptance_criteria:
Owner H0/A0 approval and the #905 additive-v2 authority amendment are recorded on the epic before G1 is undeferred.
Only G1 is undeferred at H0; every other implementation bead remains dependency-blocked.
G1 and AH0 complete sequentially, then MIG-WS, MIG-CORE, MIG-CLI, MIG-PG, and MIG-DEL complete with their alignment scans, exact proof recipes, and existing suites green.
V0 proof is Level B only: bounded replay, process-lifetime idempotency/admission, legacy wire/transcript goldens, multi-Workspace/multi-Agent/multi-storage/multi-actor isolation, shared Environment, deterministic no-journal rename, and bounded shutdown.
No durable-ledger crash matrix, durable activity checkpoint, snapshot-registry pagination, or remote-wire runtime event validator is required to close this v0 epic.

title: 909 G1 — freeze AgentGateway v0 contract and conformance
description:
## Background
G1 is the first implementation slice after H0. It freezes the placement-independent `AgentGateway` v0 semantic contract, stable errors, server-only admission and request-ledger contracts, and a reusable conformance suite. It changes no production runtime behavior.

## Changed paths
- `packages/agent/src/shared/gateway/types.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/shared/gateway/errors.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/shared/gateway/events.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/shared/gateway/__tests__/dtoDiscipline.test.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/shared/index.ts`
- Agent package export declarations in `packages/agent/package.json`
- `packages/agent/src/server/agent-host/types.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/server/agent-host/testing/gatewayConformance.ts` (new file)
- `packages/agent/src/server/agent-host/testing/__tests__/gatewayConformance.test.ts` (new file)

## Technical approach
Define the complete addressed contract: verified and authorized scope types; Agent catalog and session references; keyset session pages; create, connect, read, rename, and delete inputs; prompt and follow-up commands; interrupt, stop, and queue-clear controls; typed receipts; snapshots; connections; Gateway lifecycle; JSON-safe event envelopes with one `seq`; and every stable v0 error.

Keep `AuthorizedAgentScope` non-serializable and issuer-owned. The verifier must reject casts, spread copies, JSON round trips, capabilities from another issuer, stale membership, and revoked membership. Reverify every operation and every command on an open connection.

Define server-only `AgentGatewayEffect`, target, key, failure, record, admission, and `AgentRequestLedger` types with exact transitions: missing to pending admission; accepted admission to in flight; strong rejection before effect; legacy observed rejection from in flight; completion; and outcome unknown. The Level-B fake is process-lifetime only.

The DTO guard is structural and type-level. Do not implement recursive runtime event-leaf validation or immutable snapshot pagination. Those are v2 and Level-D responsibilities. Parameterize pagination conformance separately from replay level and specify owner-annotated Level-D skips.

## Test plan
The throwaway in-memory fake must compile and run the reusable conformance suite. Cover scope provenance, current membership, stable error mapping, every valid and invalid ledger transition, same-request retry, conflicting digest, cross-scope and cross-target request IDs, command-state transitions, close-is-unsubscribe, monotonic sequence, bounded replay gap recovery, snapshot consistency, total session order, cursor tamper and binding denial, moved-row behavior, deleted-row behavior, and a valid cursor yielding an empty page. Assert that Level-D restart, durable-ledger, durable-activity, immutable-snapshot, and remote-wire cases are named and skipped with owner annotations.

## Runnable proof recipe
Run from repository root:
1. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent typecheck`
2. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent exec vitest run src/server/agent-host/testing/__tests__/gatewayConformance.test.ts`
3. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent lint:invariants`
4. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent build`
5. `git diff --check`

Expected result: every command exits zero, shared exports resolve, invariant checks find no `node:*` or `Buffer` use, and the conformance output names all deferred cases. Manual and E2E proof are not applicable because G1 changes no production behavior. Attach command results and the exact skip list to the current-head proof comment.

## Rollback
Revert the G1 pull request before AH0 starts. No data or wire migration exists.

## Considerations
Do not leak arbitrary legacy admission codes into the closed public Gateway error union. Do not confuse `PiChatSnapshot` wire status with the coarse session-list activity status. Do not add `hostId`, provider details, roots, Fastify, Pi SDK, or live objects to shared DTOs.

## Acceptance Criteria
The canonical closure criteria are in this bead's acceptance-criteria field and are mandatory.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic contains dated H0/A0 approval before this bead changes from deferred.
All shared gateway types and stable errors compile and export from `@hachej/boring-agent/shared`; server-only admission/ledger types remain under agent-host.
AuthorizedAgentScope forgery, spread/JSON copy, cross-issuer use, and stale membership fail closed on every operation and open-connection command.
The exact effect/target/key/failure/ledger state machine compiles and passes all valid/invalid CAS transition tests against the in-memory Level-B fake.
Level B conformance passes; every durable/restart/snapshot-registry/activity case is explicitly Level D/v2-skipped with owner annotation.
Keyset tests cover binding/tamper denial plus mutation behavior: moved rows may shift, deleted rows disappear, and a still-valid cursor may yield an empty page.
No recursive runtime event validator or immutable snapshot registry is implemented in G1.
All five proof commands exit 0 and the current-PR-head proof comment records outputs and named skips.

title: 909 follow-up — activate durable request ledger and activity state
description:
## Background
The durable streaming core establishes restart-stable event offsets. This dependent follow-up activates the owner-descoped durable request ledger and durable activity state required for full Level D.

## Changed paths

- `packages/agent/src/server/agent-host/testing/__tests__/durableActivity.test.ts` (new file)

## Technical approach
Make the durable request ledger beside `sessionRoot` the Level-D default. Preserve exact prepare, admission acceptance, effect begin, rejection, completion, and outcome-unknown transitions. Replay terminal results after restart, retain completed records and create tombstones for at least 24 hours, reconcile externally accepted admission by full key, and never repeat unresolved in-flight effects.

Persist activity checkpoints with event and effect ownership. Before serving after restart, reconcile stale `running` or `aborting` records to `error`; never create a phantom or second writer.

Level-D guarantees apply only to requests admitted after activation. Activation occurs across a Host restart, so a pre-Level-D request ID retried afterward is a documented new admission. Do not implement immutable snapshot-registry pagination here.

## Runnable proof recipe
1. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent exec vitest run src/server/agent-host/testing/__tests__/durableLedgerConformance.test.ts`
2. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent exec vitest run src/server/agent-host/testing/__tests__/levelDUpgrade.test.ts`

5. `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent typecheck && pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent test && pnpm lint:invariants && git diff --check`

The first three paths are new files created by this bead; the fourth is created by AH0.

Manual fault proof: run a Host on a temporary durable session root and terminate it separately after admission acceptance, after effect begin, and after effect completion but before acknowledgement. Restart after each boundary and verify reconciliation versus terminal outcome unknown. Also verify the pre-Level-D retry case and stale activity reconciliation.

## Rollback
Restart into streaming-core Level B and document that cross-restart request guarantees are reduced. Preserve durable files and do not silently reinterpret their records.

## Considerations
Transport DTOs never expose ledger or checkpoint metadata. Retention configuration may increase but not reduce the 24-hour floor.

## Acceptance Criteria
The canonical closure criteria are in this bead's acceptance-criteria field and are mandatory.
acceptance_criteria:
The Level-D default ledger is durable beside sessionRoot, preserves exact state transitions, replays terminal results after restart, retains completed/create tombstones for at least 24h, and never repeats unresolved in-flight effects.
Durable activity checkpoints reconcile stale running/aborting to error before serving and cannot create a phantom/second writer.
The crash-boundary matrix distinguishes external-admission reconciliation from true unknown effect outcome.
The pre-Level-D requestId retry case treats the first post-upgrade attempt as a documented new admission; only requests admitted at Level D receive durable guarantees.
Snapshot-registry pagination remains explicitly out of scope/skipped.
All five proof groups and manual crash/upgrade matrix have expected results in the current-head PR proof comment; rollback leaves durable files intact and documents reduced guarantees.

description:
## Background
MIG-DEL moves `workspaceAgentDispatcher`, `managedAgentDelegate`, and Automation's `ManualRunExecutor` from the older `Agent.send` and `Agent.stream` facade to injected `AgentGateway` operations. It also implements Automation run's durable two-step saga.

## Technical approach

Preserve typed receipts, stable errors, cancellation, progress, and one native session writer. Leave the old facade and duplicate buffer definitions as compatibility code for the later owner-gated contraction bead.

Automation run is a durable two-step saga. Persist the run record and invocation-to-run receipt in the Automation store before dispatch. Derive the Gateway `requestId` from the run ID. Mark the record dispatching, perform Gateway dispatch, and persist the dispatch receipt. If the process restarts while dispatching without a receipt, resolve the run to terminal `outcome-unknown` and never automatically redispatch it. Only an explicit new run may dispatch again. This safety comes from the durable run record, not from cross-restart Level-B Gateway replay.

title: SQLITE_BUSY: use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for durable-store writes
description: Follow-up from PR #1128 review (MED residual): busy_timeout=5000 does NOT cover the real contention shape. runTransaction issues a deferred BEGIN (sqlStorage.ts:49) and appendEventOnce reads (readIdempotencyKey SELECT) then writes inside it (eventStreamStore.ts:117-135). On a deferred read->write lock upgrade SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY IMMEDIATELY, ignoring busy_timeout. Concurrent appends from two runtime bindings can therefore reach publishChannelEvents' poison policy and KILL a live channel. FIX: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write transactions. PROOF: concurrent-append test across two store instances over one file, no channel poisoned. MUST land before the flag is enabled in production.

title: Connect-time SSRF enforcement for user-registered MCP
description: The syntactic hostname/IP-literal pre-filter in plugins/boring-mcp/src/shared/index.ts (validateUserRegisteredMcpEndpoint) is NOT an SSRF control: it never resolves DNS, so an attacker A-record (e.g. 127.0.0.1.nip.io, or DNS rebinding) bypasses it entirely, and a validated https:// endpoint can still 302-redirect to a private/metadata address. mcpSdkTransport.ts now sets requestInit.redirect='error' for user-registered sources as a stopgap, but that only blocks redirects — it does not stop a first-hop connection to an attacker-controlled DNS name that resolves to a private IP. Real connect-time SSRF enforcement requires one of: (1) resolve-then-pin — resolve the hostname to an IP before connecting, re-run the private/metadata blocklist against the resolved IP, and pin the TCP connection to that IP (so a TOCTOU re-resolution can't swap it), or (2) route all user-registered MCP traffic through an egress allowlist/proxy that enforces network-level isolation from cloud metadata services and internal ranges. This must land before any user-registered MCP source is admitted in an environment that can reach production networks or a cloud metadata service.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Round-2 review residuals to fold into connect-time enforcement (all LOW *because* the pre-filter now correctly disclaims being an SSRF control): (a) IPv4-COMPATIBLE ::7f00:1 / ::127.0.0.1 still pass (distinct from IPv4-mapped, still routes to loopback on some stacks); (b) 6to4 only blocks the literal 2002:7f00:1: — 2002:a9fe:a9fe::1 (=169.254.169.254), 2002:0a00:1::1 (=10.0.0.1), 2002:c0a8:1::1 all ALLOWED; (c) NAT64 with RFC8215 non-well-known prefix 64:ff9b:1::7f00:1 passes; (d) ff00::1 multicast passes. Connect-time resolve-then-pin makes all of these moot — do not chase them in the string filter.

title: KEY0: decide model-key policy (BYOK per workspace v1)
description: Decision-shaped, plan-only bead per Decision 26 (docs/DECISIONS.md). Resolve issue #820 (#391 child): whose key pays for a tenant workspace's model calls. Proposed v1: BYOK per workspace, tenant provider keys stored via the existing encrypted workspace-settings path (WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY), injected per-execution, never baked into sandbox images; instance env key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) remains the fallback/self-host mode. Platform-billed pooled keys deferred until billing exists (#809/BL1), with observability metering (#819) as its prerequisite. Outcome: a Decision entry in docs/DECISIONS.md plus an identified config seam. No implementation before Step 1A lands. Issue: #820.

title: 16f.1 BYOK credential-injection CONTRACT + provider-registry seam
description:
Contract-first, ships in v1. Land the typed secret-reference + (workspaceId,providerId)->credential resolve interface and the provider registry seam: versioned provider/field/ref/resolver/opaque-authority(WorkspaceCredentialAuthorityVerifierV1)/lease/error types, the (deferred-Tier-2) SandboxCredential payload/callback/receipt types, host-owned trust/delivery rules, and the Tier-1 HOST-SIDE RESOLUTION path (trusted first-party => delivery host-only; key never enters sandbox). No storage, no wire implementation, no plaintext.

THIS bead is the seam SBX1.1 (#855) reconciles its stub against: SBX1.1 stubs the ref/resolver callback now and the vault implementation (16f.2/16f.5) lands behind it. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20 (amendments A/D/E) per docs/issues/820/byok-secret-vault-plan.md.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Contract and registry'): a standalone SBX1 fake compiles against this, accepts a typed reference/delivery request + fake payload-resolver callback, rejects model/host-only delivery into sandbox, validates bounded payload identities, emits a value-free receipt, returns stable CREDENTIAL_* errors without importing a vault/store impl; registry tests validate every provider/field ID, OAuth URL/scope, consumer binding, host-assigned trust/purpose/allowed-field/delivery/channel/egress at startup; OAuth registry rejects missing/public/duplicate/oversized refresh/access fields and bindings cannot request the refresh field; external-managed rejects token fields and non-host delivery; tenant input/model output/command text cannot create or widen a reference; package import invariants remain green (shared has no node:*/Buffer, workspace base has zero Agent value imports).

title: 16f.2 BYOK vault storage: KmsBackend + OVH-KMS default + local-KEK fallback
description:
Add the dedicated credential schema/store and envelope crypto. Per-workspace 256-bit DEK, AAD-bound AES-256-GCM per the research brief (12-byte random nonce, 16-byte verified tag, canonical versioned AAD = workspaceId:credentialId:providerId:fieldId:credentialVersion:dekGeneration). KmsBackend abstraction (WorkspaceKekProviderV1: generateDataKey/unwrapDataKey/rewrapDataKey/readiness, fail-closed-on-unavailable) with OVHcloud KMS as the DEFAULT managed-EU-KMS impl (external-kms-opaque.v1 payload; REST/KMIP client-cert auth; region-pinned) and an explicit LOCAL-KEK dev fallback (sealed host file, separate from DB). Scaleway/Exoscale are alternate managed-EU-KMS impls of the same interface; self-run Vault/OpenBao Transit is optional. Dev-infra Vault at 100.77.36.113 is NOT prod. Write-only/masked (last-4 metadata only), timing-safe comparisons, no-secrets-in-logs, query logging disabled for credential tables. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20 amendment A.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Cryptographic conformance'): raw Postgres inspection finds no plaintext canary/DEK/KEK/OAuth code-or-token/auth header; known-answer/round-trip per backend; corrupt ciphertext/nonce/tag/AAD/EDK/backend-ID/key-ref/key-version each independently fail closed CREDENTIAL_UNREADABLE/backend error (never 'absent'); nonce-uniqueness assertion + forbid zero/static nonce and unauthenticated modes; workspace-A row/EDK copied to B, provider-A->B, field-A->B, version-A->B all fail auth; wrong/missing KMS/local key is unreadable and never triggers another backend or instance fallback; backend conformance for OVH-KMS primary and local-KEK (sealed-file fixture, verified wrapper tag, rotation/rewrap, startup failure without key, no env fallback).

title: 16f.3 BYOK onboarding flow: provider registry + API-key + OAuth
description:
Generalize the MCP provider overlay into an owner-only 'Providers & credentials' workspace-settings surface. Provider registry + API-key onboarding (write-only forms; response returns state/version/timestamps/account label + masked last-4 only; form clears after submit) + OAuth authorization-code with PKCE and server-side refresh (local-vault custody: refresh token encrypted through the same envelope pipeline, access token memory-only; external-managed custody: store only bounded account reference, no fictitious token). Dedicated owner-authorized routes; generic /settings rejects reserved credential names. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Authorization and API' + 'OAuth'): owner may create/replace/connect/disable/revoke, editor/viewer/nonmember cannot; GET/list/status/callback responses carry metadata + last-4 only (canary scans reject secret/ciphertext/EDK/token); a plain/copied/expired/cast fake cannot pass the Core authority verifier; membership removed after queue but before dispatch denies resolve; rate/body/CSRF/idempotency/concurrent-version-swap covered and idempotency stores no secret body; exact redirect/state/PKCE/short-TTL/atomic-consume/replay/cross-workspace-callback/initiator-lost-owner/denied-scope/provider-error/popup-cancel covered; refresh encrypted via envelope, access memory-only, rotating refresh atomically supersedes old version under concurrency; invalid_grant => needs-reauth without fallback.

title: 16f.4 BYOK MCP generalization onto shared mechanism (+ pi MCP edge reuse)
description:
Migrate @hachej/boring-mcp onboarding/state/server adapter onto the shared workspace provider-credential mechanism; do not ship a parallel BYOK onboarding surface. Move MCP connection authority from per-user __serverBoringMcpSourcesV1 metadata to the workspace provider-credential record; createdByUserId becomes audit-only. Consent-quarantine per decision #6: never auto-promote a personal connection; quarantine collisions; require connected-user consent + current-owner approval/reconnection. Adapt ManagedConnectorSecretResolver to the generic host-side resolver; operator Composio key stays operator-owned. Amendment E: REUSE pi's MCP connection/auth edge (pi already owns MCP client connection+auth) rather than duplicating it; inventory pi's MCP-connection surface first. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20.

Acceptance gates (plan 'OAuth'/MCP migration + 'MCP and per-consumer integration'): seed two users in one workspace with the same provider and prove neither account is promoted/selected automatically; require connected-user consent plus current-owner approval/reconnection; reject a departed-user promotion; preserve personal authority on rollback; preserve origin allowlisting, source status, revoke verification, readonly tool policy, response redaction, and secret-canary gates; MCP result passes existing readonly/redaction policy.

title: 16f.5 BYOK first-party proxy tools (Tier-1 host-side: web-search + transcription)
description:
Tier-1 host-side resolution (amendment D). Register Tavily/Firecrawl (web-search) and Deepgram/Whisper (transcription) and wire them to resolve the credential HOST-SIDE via the 16f.1 contract, make the outbound provider call from the host, and return only sanitized results/transcript/artifacts. The secret NEVER enters the sandbox. Covers the owner's actual v1 needs (first-party web-search + transcription; model keys follow the same host-only pattern). Local/public Whisper uses provider 'none'. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Host and cross-tenant resolution' + consumer matrix): resolve immediately before the outbound call and dispose lease in finally; two workspaces x >=2 providers x concurrent search/transcription calls observe only their matching canaries at the final fake-provider boundary; host proxy results contain no secret in headers/body/errors/logs/events/sessions/traces; search/transcription keys never enter Sandbox exec; tombstone blocks the next resolve immediately.

title: 16f.6 (DEFERRED) BYOK in-sandbox injection (Tier-2, untrusted custom tools)
description:
DEFERRED (amendment D). The ONLY path that delivers a secret INTO the sandbox, for untrusted tenant custom tools (tenant 'user repo' code needing a credential). Delivery via stdin/pipe (FD 3) or per-execution tmpfs; NEVER env/argv/image/common-create-context. Not built in v1; deferred until a tenant actually authors a credential-using custom tool. GATED behind (a) a hostile-test harness (plant a canary secret; assert it never appears in sandbox env, /proc/*/environ, ps, argv, docker inspect/config/labels, image/history/layers, durable /workspace, logs; assert a cross-workspace probe cannot read another workspace's injected secret; mirror the runsc qualification-harness approach) PLUS (b) a red-team pass on the contract before implementation. Pairs with SBX1 wt-391-forward-6gd.3 for concrete worker-to-child FD3/tmpfs delivery + teardown.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Sandbox delivery'): two-workspace x two-sandbox cross-product rejects mismatched refs before decrypt; authenticated sandboxId<->workspaceId receipt mandatory; canary available only on FD3/fixed-tmpfs to the intended process and absent from every sink above; success/provider-error/handler-error/timeout/abort/fork/double-fork/worker-disconnect all close/unmount/clear and uncertain cleanup destroys the container and blocks reuse; remains disabled under network-none until per-provider egress + fresh SBX1 isolation/exfiltration qualification pass; positive control proves the intended tenant process can read its own credential and call only the allowed fake endpoint.
notes: DESIGN GUIDANCE (from sandbox-provider injection research, 2026-07-22): The in-sandbox delivery mechanism for Tier-2 should follow the industry standard, which corrects an earlier 'prefer stdin/tmpfs' note. BASELINE = env-var-at-creation, per-workspace, injected from the control-plane vault at sandbox boot — this is what E2B, Modal, Vercel (our current sandbox), Fly, and Cloudflare all do. Env vars are acceptable here because the sandbox is single-tenant and the secret belongs to that tenant; cross-tenant safety rests ENTIRELY on gVisor isolation strength (the SBX1.2 qualification), NOT on env-var hiding. OWASP's 'no secrets in env vars' targets shared multi-app hosts and does not apply to a single-tenant isolated sandbox where the sandbox owner = secret owner. PREMIUM OPTION (evaluate for the external-service/standalone-sandbox tier where the code author is NOT the key owner): Daytona-style egress-proxy brokering — the env var holds an opaque PLACEHOLDER and the real value is substituted at the network egress proxy for allow-listed hosts, so the key never enters the sandbox and code cannot read/exfiltrate it. This is the correct form of a 'vault broker' (swap-at-egress, not fetch-from-inside). CAVEATS to design around: (1) the daemon/injector sees plaintext at boot — minimize the trusted injector, scope decryption to boot, drop access on teardown (Fly model); store keys encrypted at rest in the control-plane vault (KMS envelope), never in images/snapshots; (2) env persists for the sandbox lifetime and is readable by any code run — accepted for BYOK (tenant's own key = residual #7), but for untrusted-to-the-tenant code use the egress-proxy; (3) persistent/snapshotted sandboxes (Vercel persistence is default) may capture env state — EXCLUDE secrets from snapshots or re-inject at resume. Still gated behind the canary/leak-invariant hostile-test harness + red-team before implementation.

title: 16f.7 BYOK migration off WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
description:
Inventoried migration off the legacy app-wide WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY credential path (decision #11). Inventory every workspace_settings key and MCP __serverBoringMcpSourcesV1 record; classify metadata vs credential material. For a legacy encrypted credential: decrypt once with the legacy key, encrypt into the new per-workspace envelope, verify via the new resolver/provider probe, dispose, then atomically switch that workspace/provider read pointer. Never dual-write plaintext. Tombstone/quarantine migrated rows. Retire the legacy credential path only after a full rollback window and backup-retention + owner approval; it may remain temporarily for unrelated legacy settings but is never a vault fallback. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20.

Acceptance gates (plan 'Migration and rollout' + 'Lifecycle and operational proof'): verify each migrated envelope before switching reads; never dual-write secret values; rollback restores the previous safe path only and never converts new ciphertext back to plaintext; a credential already migrated is never decrypted back into generic settings; retire WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY for credentials only after backup-retention + owner approval.

title: D1-004d1 admission ledger core
description:
## Goal and why
D1-004d1 admission ledger core: add the durable Postgres admission ledger foundation — Drizzle migration/schema, admissionLedger.ts, session advisory fence, and CLI destructive-diff read — keyed by host, binding, and execution identity. Commit before effects, use advisory fencing, and fail closed on mismatch or commit failure. This is the reusable admission ledger core; it does not own consumer wiring or rollback journaling.

## Scope
One reviewable PR. ≤400 net lines. Preserve Decisions 21–24, workspace-first authority, and no pure mode. Scope is narrowed to the ledger core only: Drizzle migration/schema + admissionLedger.ts + session advisory fence + CLI destructive-diff read. D1-004d2 owns Pi first-effect admission consumers; D1-004d3 owns the WorkspaceBridge operation admission seam. D1-004e owns append-only rollback-journal creation, prepared-state reads, and recovery fencing. D1-005c is the first concrete stable-core consumer of the admission hook.

## Explicit exclusions
No rollback-journal reads or writes, publication pointer, served acknowledgement, scheduler, queue, registry/provisioner, control plane, generic policy framework, secret/raw-path output, or unrelated refactor. No Pi service decorator, createAgent.ts facade, slash/reload hook wiring, or WorkspaceBridge operation wiring (those are D1-004d2/d3).

## Acceptance and proof
Focused unit tests prove admission rows and advisory fencing commit before the first effect and reject a mismatch/commit failure without effects. Run targeted typecheck/tests and attach redacted output.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance field: focused proof verifies only this bead's owned contract.

Acceptance Criteria:
Focused proof verifies: admitted binding remains non-removable after process restart and revision-directory cleanup; landing-only revisions preserve execution identity; binding-id reuse with different execution facts fails closed; concurrent admission is idempotent; kill-after-commit-before-effect leaves a deliberate permanent fence; and pre-commit/lock failure produces no effect. No rollback journal or stable-core publication behavior is implemented.

Owned stable codes: D1_ADMISSION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, D1_ADMISSION_RECORD_FAILED (must match these names exactly — do not invent variants).

Split per sizing audit 2026-07-13; siblings D1-004d2/d3 carry the consumer seams (pre-declared in PR-PLAN).

title: Orchestrator tick needs a run duration cap — a wedged tick silently stops the factory
description:
Gap identified 2026-08-21 while reviewing PR #1288. Nothing can recover a stuck orchestrator: the cron cannot nudge it (each tick starts a FRESH session; sessionMode continue was cut), RUN_ALREADY_ACTIVE SKIPS every subsequent tick while the wedged run stays active, and the nudge ladder points orchestrator->workers only, never at itself. Net effect: one hung tick = the factory silently stops supervising while looking healthy (no error, one active run, gates just stop arriving). This is exactly how both epic orchestrators died on 2026-08-15/16 and why a human has been the de facto watchdog all week.

FIX: give the orchestrator automation a run duration cap (e.g. 3x its interval); on breach, terminate the run so the next tick starts. Safe because ticks are idempotent by design — they re-derive leases, runs and the ready queue from beads, so killing one loses nothing. Complement with the already-planned drain alarm (no completed tick in N minutes -> one owner intention).

Deliberately NOT added to PR #1288 (owner priority: ship the factory's last blocker; it had already been through 4 review rounds). This is the first thing the factory should fix about itself once running.

title: GH-579 Markdown recording shelf production integration
description:
## Goal
Deliver the production Markdown recording shelf approved by the GH-579 spike through three bounded phases: safe recording read APIs, protected Tiptap association, and a fully collapsible multi-recording shelf with one workspace playback owner.

## Background
Users need dictated transcript prose to feel like normal Markdown while retaining a clear association with locally retained audio. Audio and status belong in one collapsible editor-owned shelf; transcript headings, paragraphs, and lists remain ordinary editable Tiptap content. The complete list must collapse, playback must continue safely while collapsed, and microphone capture must take priority over playback.

## Locked V1 scope
- Exact-document inventory is capped at 50; no pagination or ETag.
- Audio reads return one complete bounded manifest-owned chunk; no Range support.
- Existing T11 begin/end sentinels remain the serialized format; no migration.
- Collapse state is local to the mounted editor and is not persisted.
- Association removal, inline audio nodes, word synchronization, waveform editing, and hosted STT migration are excluded.
- No backend document writer and no recording metadata on ordinary transcript prose.

## Dependency shape
T15 read API beads feed T16 Tiptap association and T17 playback. T16 and playback/polling converge in the T17 shelf. The final integration proof blocks the existing T14 ship gate.

## Definition of done
Every child bead meets its acceptance checklist, exact gates, evidence requirement, and cross-provider review. The graph has no cycles, package boundaries remain intact, guarded giant files do not gain orchestration, and final browser proof covers real multi-chunk audio at desktop and mobile widths.

## Evidence
Each child records commands, outputs, pass/fail, changed files, residual risks, and review result in bead comments. No private microphone audio, transcript content, tokens, or internal artifact paths enter committed evidence.\n\n## Frozen shared-file ownership map
- recordingApiClient inventory list/DTO decode: .14 only.
- recordingApiClient complete-chunk binary/header parser: .12 only, after .14.
- .13/.15/.17/.21 are import-only consumers and may not call status() for shelf/playback.
- RecordingManifest/manifestStore/recordingStore create/list seams: .2 only; .4 consumes the exported lookup.
- recordings.ts and shared routes.test.ts extraction: .20 only; .3/.4 own disjoint modules/tests.
- MarkdownEditor mount extraction: .18 only; atomic extension/completion cutover: .9 only; shelf uses the extracted seam.

## Review RACI
Per-bead review checks diff+acceptance only. .5 and .11 check phase seam compatibility and cite focused dispositions without re-litigation absent failing evidence. .19 checks the frozen tree, maintainability, privacy/security, and aggregate regression evidence.

## Frozen provider mount ownership
- .14 alone mounts RecordingInventoryStore in existing TranscriptionProvider and owns its provider-file edit.
- .12 runs after .14 and alone inserts PlaybackProvider as a focused child; it does not restructure/remount the provider.
- .13 runs after .12 and owns only controller coordinator injection plus ComposerDictationAdapter callback wiring.
- .21 must not edit either provider file; it owns only resolver consumer/lifecycle registration.
- .15/.17/.22/.24 are provider/client import-only consumers.

## Review commands and inputs
- Per-bead: implementation diff + bead acceptance + exact gate evidence; first-level GPT-5.5 high and independent Sol final review, fix/repeat until clean.
- Phase .5/.11: phase diffs, focused dispositions, and seam-compatibility evidence only; no product re-litigation absent a failing gate.
- Final .19: exact frozen tree, all phase dispositions, thermonuclear maintainability, privacy/security, and aggregate regression evidence.
- Plan/bead architecture: Grok + Claude Opus CLI + Gemini adversarial panel; accepted findings are fixed and rerun when provider capacity permits.

title: GH-579 T15a define bounded recording-read contracts
description:
## Goal
Define browser-safe shared contracts and stable errors for fixed-limit exact-document recording inventory plus complete bounded audio-chunk reads.

## Background
The shelf needs safe metadata and deterministic candidate-chunk selection without sidecar paths, capture credentials, an unbounded timeline, pagination, ETag, Range, or a second playback-plan endpoint.

## Scope
- Define GET document-recordings request/response types for one supported existing documentPath: .md, .markdown, .txt, or .text.
- Return at most 50 newest-first items plus truncated.
- Each item contains recording id; stable 1-based ordinal; lifecycle; start/end/duration; transcript version; immutable create-time rolling chunkDurationMs; chunk count; recording-level audio availability/deletion state; and safe failure code.
- Define ordinal as the rank over all retained manifests ordered (createdAt ASC, recordingId ASC); newest-first projection and truncation never renumber it.
- Define provenance: new manifests persist create-time chunkDurationMs; legacy manifests derive a read-only maximum-positive-saved-span fallback and are never rewritten. No usable timing yields a stable playback-unavailable reason, never current server policy.
- Define complete-chunk response/error metadata for recordingId plus integer index, including shared constants/parser for Content-Type, Content-Length, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Index, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Start-Ms, and X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-End-Ms.
- Reuse existing TRANSCRIPTION_RECORDING_AUDIO_MISSING for unavailable/missing/deleted chunk audio and existing auth/not-found/bounds errors; do not add a second audio-unavailable code and keep shared code free of node imports and Buffer. out_of_inventory is exclusively a T17 client snapshot state, never an HTTP error; retained recording-id audio reads remain valid outside the newest-50 projection.

## Non-goals
No store/route implementation, audio bytes, UI, playback, Tiptap, per-chunk array, pagination, ETag, Range, playback-plan endpoint, or document mutation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Types encode every field/provenance/ordinal rule above and exclude secrets, paths, transcript body, hashes, and provider details.
- [ ] Fixtures cover Markdown/plain-text paths, lifecycle/audio states, legacy timing fallback, unusable timing, truncation without renumbering, and malformed input.
- [ ] Existing API compatibility is preserved.

## Gate commands
- pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-transcription typecheck
- pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-transcription test
Pass means both exit 0 with focused shared-contract tests.

## Evidence
Record exported types/errors, synthetic examples, legacy fallback/ordinal fixtures, test names, and browser-safe source proof.

## Required completion record
- [ ] Implementation stays inside the stated ownership boundary.
- [ ] Exact gates pass, or a concrete skip reason and replacement evidence is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence contains commands, relevant output, changed files, residual risks, and assignment token.
- [ ] Architecture/docs are updated for public seams, otherwise N/A is recorded.
- [ ] Focused cross-provider review passes; fix and repeat until clean before STATE impl:done.

Never record secrets, private transcript/audio content, tokens, Authorization headers, or internal artifact paths. Preserve unrelated changes, stable errors, package/workspace isolation, and giant-file guards.\n\n## Preflight fail-closed gate
Before impl:start, verify plugins/boring-transcription/src/shared/errors.ts, shared/types.ts, server/recordings/types.ts, and the merged T06/T09 recording store/worker tests exist. Stop rather than invent a parallel contract if absent.
notes: Contract correction: inventory items expose immutable rolling chunkDurationMs, chunkCount, total/end duration, and recording-level availability, but no unbounded per-chunk array. Complete-chunk responses expose safe index/start/end timing metadata. No playback-plan endpoint, pagination, ETag, or Range.

title: GH-579 T16e expose workspace-isolated marker navigation registry
description:
## Goal
Expose a narrow editor-owned association registry so T17 can navigate recording id to marker and marker activation back to a shelf row without importing private editor internals or querying the global DOM.

## Background
Multiple workspaces/editors may open identical document paths. Navigation must be provider-scoped and panel-aware, following the existing filesystem open-editor/action registry pattern.

## Scope
- Register/unregister mounted marker targets by workspace/editor identity, document path, recording id, and panel id.
- Expose typed focus/scroll-to-marker command with reduced-motion behavior.
- Emit typed marker-activation intent for the owning shelf.
- Define deterministic behavior for multiple panes of the same document.
- Clean up on unmount, path change, workspace switch, and plugin removal.
- Add keyboard activation and screen-reader announcement contract.

## Non-goals
No shelf UI, audio, polling, controller ownership, global document query, or generic workspace-plugin manifest field.

title: GH-579 T17a implement bounded multi-chunk playback owner
description:
## Goal
Implement one workspace playback owner that sequences one bounded T15 audio chunk at a time for one active recording.

## Background
V1 uses immutable rolling chunkDurationMs plus manifest-owned timing returned with each chunk; it has no unbounded timeline, Range request, or all-chunk preload.

## Scope

- Consume T15 inventory snapshot fields and complete-chunk endpoint only; never status sidecarPath/hash fields.
- Compute candidate index from chunkDurationMs, fetch one chunk, validate returned index/start/end timing, and map local/recording elapsed time.
- Sequence on ended and seek across chunks; missing/failed/deleted candidate becomes explicit unavailable and is never silently skipped.
- Maintain one audio element/current Blob/object URL; revoke on transition, stop, error, unmount, path/workspace switch, or replacement playback.
- Pause previous playback before starting another; deduplicate requests and ignore stale responses.
- Consume the T17c immutable availability snapshot. If active id disappears, transition to out_of_inventory, pause/stop, revoke resources, and refuse auto-advance while its marker retains neutral recording-id navigation.

## Non-goals
No polling implementation, capture arbitration, shelf UI, Tiptap, Range, preload, waveform, trimming, word sync, or persistence.

- [ ] Candidate selection, timing validation, transition, and cross-chunk seek preserve elapsed time.
- [ ] Every replacement/teardown/error/out-of-inventory path revokes deterministically.
- [ ] Missing/deleted/failed/out-of-inventory is explicit and never skipped.
- [ ] Playback does not create its own inventory polling loop.

## Goal
Expose an authenticated complete-chunk audio read resolved only through the canonical recording manifest.

## Background
Long-recording chunks are independently decodable and bounded by the configured maximum. V1 playback fetches one whole chunk Blob at a time, avoiding Range and aggregate-audio complexity.

## Scope
- Implement GET /api/v1/transcription/document-recordings/:recordingId/audio/:chunkIndex.
- Validate recording id and non-negative integer chunk index.
- Resolve audio only through the canonical manifest and Workspace-safe binary read seam.
- Require authenticated workspace authority, not the expired capture owner token.
- Return complete bytes with stored Content-Type and accurate Content-Length plus X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Index, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Start-Ms, and X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-End-Ms from the exact manifest entry, using only T15a shared constants/parser.
- Reject unsaved, failed, missing, deleted, oversized, or wrong-workspace audio with stable errors.
- Redact request/access logs and never accept an arbitrary path.

## Non-goals
No Range, cache validator, streaming concatenation, transcoding, preload, playback UI, or retention change.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Valid synthetic WebM bytes round-trip exactly with Content-Type, Content-Length, and exact index/start/end timing headers.
- [ ] Invalid/deleted/missing/failed/oversized/cross-workspace cases fail before bytes are exposed.
- [ ] Route tests prove no path or token can influence file selection.

worker-970-round1: Sol thermo review round2 complete on review/938-package-skill-resources, forward-merged into review/942-readonly-workspace-paths. Pushed both.

Per-item status:

1. NAMED-FS ROOT (finding 5, probe-proven incomplete) — FIXED. Root cause: round-1's routeAllMounts returned each mount's RoutedPath with logicalPath="" (the ancestor prefix) instead of the mount's own full logicalRoot, so walkFiles recursion built the wrong child path for the first descendant; and stat/find/grep never checked for virtual-ancestor directories (only list did), so stat("packages")/find("/")/grep("/") all threw READONLY_PROJECTION_INVALID_PATH even though list("/") worked. Fixed by:
   - routeUnion(handle, logicalPath): returns RoutedPath entries with each mount's full logicalRoot preserved, for any logicalPath that is an ancestor of one or more mounts (root "" included).
   - routeTraversalTargets(handle, logicalPath): tries the exact single-mount route first, falls back to routeUnion when that fails and the path is a virtual ancestor.
   - stat() and list() both now check routeUnion as a fallback: stat reports isDirectory:true for any virtual ancestor, list synthesizes its next-segment children.
   - find()/grep() now call routeTraversalTargets instead of the round-1 routeAllMounts (which only handled the exact root case).
   Added packages/boring-bash/src/server/__tests__/agentResourceRoutes.test.ts — route-level tests exercising the real agent_resources binding through the actual tree.ts and search.ts routes (recursive tree walk, root-find search) — because the round-1 regression slipped through operations-only unit tests that only covered list("/"). Also added a direct unit test covering stat/find/grep at root and at the virtual "packages" ancestor segment.

2. FRONTMATTER PARSER (finding 8, deferral rejected) — FIXED per Sol's compromise. Extracted packages/agent/src/server/skillFrontmatter.ts exporting parseSkillMetadataFrontmatter, which wraps @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent's parseFrontmatter (the same YAML parser routes/skills.ts's loadSkills() already uses internally) — exported from @hachej/boring-agent/server. packageResources.ts (packages/workspace) now consumes it via the pre-existing Workspace->Agent dependency edge; its hand-rolled `frontmatterValue` line-scanner is deleted. title: ID1-009 owner gate: name stock CIMD client
description:
## Goal and why
Record the concrete stock OAuth/OIDC client that requires Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), so ID1-009 is consumer-backed rather than speculative.

## Scope
Human decision/evidence gate for ID1-009 only; no runtime code.

## Required evidence
A committed decision/review record identifies the stock client, explains why DCR is insufficient and CIMD is required, links the supporting interoperability evidence, names the approver and date, and points to the authoritative path or URL.

## Explicit exclusions
No CIMD fetcher, generic client registry, or policy framework.
acceptance_criteria: No code test is expected. Close only when a committed decision/review record names the stock CIMD client, its concrete requirement, supporting evidence, authoritative path/URL, approver, and date.

title: Composer must show the model the session is actually using
description:
GH #1290.

Symptom: composer showed Kimi K2.6/Infomaniak then Sonnet 4.6 for a session that ran 160 turns on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol. Owner concluded metered keys were being burned and stopped a healthy worker.

Root cause: useChatModelSelection (packages/agent/src/front/hooks/) initialises from browser-local storage via readPiComposerSettings and never consults the session; the session state envelope has no model field at all (protocolVersion, sessionId, seq, status, messages, queue, followUpMode).

Fix: (1) surface the session's current model in the addressed state envelope; (2) front initialises the composer from the session model when opening an existing session, local storage only for NEW sessions; (3) if the viewer overrides for their next message, show that it differs rather than silently replacing the display.

Requirement from owner: the model displayed = the model the session is currently using.

title: AC1-T2 AgentTask v2 typed artifact authority
description:
## Goal and why
AC1-T2 AgentTask v2 typed artifact authority: Replace generic ArtifactRef URI authority with discriminated platform-owned opaque ArtifactLocator and publish AgentTask schema v2; edge-only v1 compatibility rejects arbitrary schemes before effects.

## Scope
Implement one coherent, reviewable PR only; preserve Decision 21–24, workspace-first authority, and the plan's no-pure-mode rule.

## Explicit exclusions
No scheduler, queue, registry/provisioner, control plane, generic policy framework, secret/raw-path output, or unrelated refactor. Do not silently widen this bead.

## Acceptance and proof
Add focused unit tests at the public seam and integration/e2e or host-proof coverage where this task crosses a runtime boundary. Run the package typecheck, targeted tests, and the exact plan acceptance gate; attach redacted command output/evidence to the PR.

## Risks / owner blockers
No generic URL locator; paths/http/file schemes must fail before network/storage effects.

## Acceptance Criteria
Focused unit coverage plus the named integration, e2e, or EU-host proof passes. Stable-code, redaction, authority, and no-widening assertions must hold before merge.
acceptance_criteria: Focused unit tests and the named integration/e2e or EU-host proof pass; all stable-code, redaction, authority, and no-widening assertions in this bead hold before merge.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STOP: recommend promoting to a small epic, not forcing into one bugfix commit.

Findings: store.ts already declares heartbeatRun/claimRunForDispatch/reconcileOrphanedRuns; fileStore.ts and postgresStore.ts implement them, but heartbeatRun is never called anywhere and reconcileOrphanedRuns only runs when a new run is next begun for that automation (dueRunService.ts:51), not on a periodic tick. postgresStore.reconcileOrphanedRuns (line 121) blanket-fails every queued/dispatching/running row for an automation with no per-run ownership check -- gh-903 explicitly flags this as unsafe for multi-replica scheduler ticks (can't distinguish a live run owned by another replica from an orphan).

A correct fix needs: a lease/owner column + DB migration (migrations.ts) on boring_automation_runs, rewired claimRunForDispatch/heartbeatRun to set/extend a lease, an actual heartbeat caller wired into hostedDueRunService.ts/hostedDueCoordinator.ts, a per-run (not per-automation) stale-lease reclaim replacing the blanket reconcile, plus tests for crash/restart, rolling-deploy overlap, and exactly-once scheduling -- all called out as required proof in gh-903 itself, which also separately asks for migration/rollout/observability/rollback design. This exceeds one reviewable commit; recommend spinning up a small epic (schema migration issue, lease/heartbeat logic issue, coordinator wiring + tests issue) rather than forcing it here.

No code changes made. Leaving status in_progress per instructions is not requested -- bead not closed, awaiting owner triage.

title: Bug: agent CSS dist wiped by JS-only rebuilds
description: BUGFIX LANE (fix/rolling): packages/agent tsup.config.ts clean:true wipes dist/front/styles.css on every JS-only rebuild because build-front-css.mjs is a separate script not wired into tsup — any 'npx tsup' leaves the package with missing CSS and downstream vite imports 500 (bit 3 agents on 2026-08-06). FIX: wire the CSS step into the build (tsup onSuccess hook, or exclude dist/front/styles.css from clean, or make 'build' the only documented entry — pick the idiom the repo uses elsewhere). PROOF: run bare npx tsup, styles.css survives or is regenerated. 1 commit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Fixed. SHA 3337907c0ac3a9ff91f66d997b9f75b29be496ce on fix/rolling.

Option chosen: A (tsup onSuccess hook), matching the idiom already used in packages/core/tsup.config.ts (which copies hand-authored CSS in onSuccess). Added onSuccess to packages/agent/tsup.config.ts that spawns scripts/build-front-css.mjs after every tsup run, so bare `npx tsup` (or watch mode) regenerates dist/front/styles.css instead of leaving it deleted by clean:true.

PROOF:
1. `npx tsup` alone (packages/agent): dist/front/styles.css exists, 158.8K (>50KB threshold). Build log shows tsup "Cleaning output folder" then completing; CSS present after.
2. `pnpm build` (tsup && build-front-css.mjs && build:assert): succeeds, build:assert prints "build-artifacts: OK". CSS step runs twice (once via onSuccess, once via the package.json script) - idempotent, no breakage, no infinite loop, ~same total time.

Cross-package note: packages/core/tsup.config.ts already has this exact pattern solved via onSuccess CSS copy - not affected. packages/workspace, packages/ui, packages/boring-bash, packages/boring-sandbox, packages/plugin-cli, packages/cli tsup configs have no separate front-CSS build step (no dist/front/styles.css analog), so they don't share this failure mode. Only packages/agent had a standalone CSS script decoupled from tsup's clean lifecycle.

title: BYOK: implement DEK-generation rotation (crypto-shred lever)
description: From PR #1132 crypto review (MEDIUM, completeness): DEK-generation rotation is NOT implemented — dekGeneration is always existing?.dekGeneration ?? 1, nothing increments it. Only KEK-level rewrapWorkspaceDek exists. The per-workspace crypto-shred lever (ratification line 70) therefore depends entirely on destroying the KMS key. Deferral is defensible but was NOT listed among deferred items. Consequence: one DEK per workspace, unbounded lifetime under random 96-bit nonces (safe at realistic volume ~2^-33 at 2^32 msgs, but removes the nonce-space reset). Implement rotation + list it honestly.

title: BYOK: credential version rollback not prevented
description: From PR #1132 crypto review (MEDIUM): AAD binds WHICH version a row is, but nothing binds WHICH version is CURRENT. An attacker with DB WRITE access can set record.credentialVersion back to an older value and a rotated-away (possibly leaked) field row decrypts cleanly. In #820's threat model (live-DB-write attacker subverts integrity) — BUT rotate-after-leak is the primary user-facing remediation and it is not cryptographically durable. FIX: monotonic/authenticated current-version marker. Do before the Postgres pass.

title: Spike: factory-in-a-sandbox — clone boring-ui into a Blaxel sandbox and run the factory there
description:
Owner ruling 2026-08-19: the pragmatic path to factory-in-Seneca-prod is NOT the plugin/workspaces-mode route — just clone boring-ui into a sandbox and run folder mode, exactly like the dev VM. This spike measures the go/no-go.

SPIKE SCOPE (timeboxed, evidence over polish):
1. Provision a Blaxel sandbox WITH a volume (boring-vol-* pattern from the merged adapter). Region eu-fra-1 worked in prior smokes.
2. Inside: git clone boring-ui (shallow ok), npx @hachej/boring-ui-cli@0.1.101 <clone> in folder mode. Record boot result, seat composition, ask_user + boring_automation presence on seats.
3. Credentials: inject a scoped gh token + one model credential the way the BYOK slices (#1145/#1164/#1166) intend — or the closest manual approximation, documenting the delta vs those PRs. NEVER bake secrets into the image/repo.
4. Egress check: github.com, registry.npmjs.org, model API reachable from inside.

7. Surface: document (not necessarily implement) how Seneca domain-routing would map factory.senecaapp.ai to the sandbox hub port.

title: Automation nudge on a busy session: no-op with recorded reason, not 409
description: Owner ruling 2026-08-21: 'if I type in the orchestrator => should queue the message.. if automation -> should just ignore'. Keep it observable (recorded reason), never a silent swallow. title: ask_user: supersede/withdraw stale intentions when re-raising gates
description:
Imported from gh#1306 (2026-08-15) during the 2026-08-26 cleanup — the issue had NO bead; this one is now canonical.
SYMPTOM: durable ask_user intentions have no supersede/withdraw lifecycle. Re-raising a gate at a new SHA leaves the stale gate actionable — one merge-gate session produced EIGHT stale merge intentions; the owner could answer an obsolete gate and the Inbox became noisy.
EXPECTED: a caller can explicitly supersede or withdraw an unanswered intention; re-raising the same correlated gate at a new SHA atomically supersedes the old one (single actionable row per correlated gate).
RELATED: gh#1348/PR #1384 (restart-safe gates + decision record) touches the same store — coordinate; C5 durable-pause absorb (boring-v2 port) is the long-term home of this lifecycle.
Original: https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/issues/1306

description:

Implement GitHub #912 only: /live start "title", /live stop, /live status; compact explicit consent; one statically composed singleton; one live session/microphone owner per workspace in one owning app process; stream-only audio to private pinned Kyutai/Moshi stt-1b-en_fr through an authenticated same-origin backend proxy; no audio retention; one timestamped non-diarized Markdown artifact read-only in the live UI; revision-safe projection at most once/second; browser socket close is terminal; only one upstream Kyutai restart; same originating chat stays usable and receives changed-only hidden reviews at +60s then +120s; exact NO_LIVE_RECOMMENDATION is suppressed. Flag remains off until final owner approval.

## Non-goals
No MediaRecorder, chunks, upload, playback, pause/resume, browser reconnect, reload/crash recovery, diarization, transcript cards, modes, provider abstraction, generic audio/WebSocket/job/hidden-turn platform, distributed lease, dynamic provider mounting, query credentials, or old recording subsystem integration. Transcript text is untrusted. Stable errors, Workspace-only file access, and repository import invariants apply.

## Scope
Create the smallest flag-off contract proof for a core/full-app-owned resolver shared by HTTP mutations and WebSocket upgrades. It must return authenticated principalId, workspaceId, chat-session authority, and resolved Workspace; reject client IDs/raw roots/local-only actor as production authority; reuse host CSRF policy for HTTP; require one canonical allowed Origin for upgrade; and prove a 256-bit hashed single-use pending-attachment capability delivered in the first strict binary message with a 15-second orphan deadline. Start/attachment capability binds principal/workspace/chat/live-session/connection; wrong scope, reuse, expiry, and same-principal competing tabs fail closed. No accepting audio route.

## Repository seams
Inspect packages/core/src/app/server/{createCoreWorkspaceAgentServer,coreWorkspaceBridge}.ts and tests; packages/workspace/src/app/server/createWorkspaceAgentServer.ts only for explicit local-only development composition. Do not widen generic external-plugin auth APIs.

## Acceptance/proof
API-level HTTP+upgrade tests cover valid auth, absent auth, membership/session mismatch, spoofed workspace headers, missing/invalid CSRF, allowed and absent/null/malformed/multi-valued/hostile Origin, attachment redemption/reuse/theft/expiry, and deadline cleanup that revision-safely interrupts when possible and releases lease/lock. Record exact production symbols and commands on issue #912. Feature flag and audio acceptance remain off.

## Status non-disclosure
Unauthorized, non-member, cross-workspace, cross-session, non-owner, spoofed and capability-only status calls reveal no active path, title, session ID, lease, capability, or upstream detail; return only stable non-secret idle/authorization results after host authority checks.
acceptance_criteria: Focused core/full-app HTTP+upgrade tests prove: (a) invalid/spoofed HTTP or upgrade authority, CSRF, Origin, and capability redemption fail before live-route Workspace operations or audio acceptance; (b) a valid pending-start expiry uses only its already resolved Workspace, revision-safely marks interrupted when expected bytes still match, revokes capability, and releases lease/lock. Cover membership/session mismatch, same-principal tab race, expiry/reuse, and redaction. Commands: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-core test; pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-core typecheck; pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace test; pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace typecheck; pnpm audit:imports; git diff --check. Record exact test paths/production symbols.

## Privacy bounds
Worklet: one frame plus bounded carry. Browser: one unsent frame. Proxy: one decoded frame plus one in-flight send. Overflow interrupts. Terminal cleanup clears references and counters to zero. Logger/persistence/crash/request spies reject PCM. No MediaRecorder/chunks/temp/audio DB/log.

44.1/48k mono/stereo deterministic worklet tests, malformed/oversized/backpressure, scripted pinned provider fixtures, paragraph cadence/dedupe/epoch timestamps, CAS conflict, start deadline, stop/idempotent cleanup and graceful interruption pass. ## Attachment and terminal contract

Wrong scope, mismatch, reuse, expiry, text framing, permission/worklet/setup loss, or missing the 15-second deadline fails closed; revision-safely mark interrupted when possible and release lease/lock. Discard a final partial audio frame on stop. Malformed provider output interrupts. Any browser close is terminal with no reconnect. Stop or failure flushes and writes complete/interrupted only while the expected revision still matches; revision conflict preserves external bytes, emits the stable conflict error, releases lease and unlocks without terminal rewrite; only upstream Kyutai may restart once.

## Runnable proof
Commands: live package test/typecheck/lint; scripted pinned-fixture tests; applicable core/workspace tests; `pnpm audit:imports`; `git diff --check`. Name exact worklet, protocol, projector, cleanup and privacy test files.

title: File surfaces need tabs: opening several files in a row shows only the last
description:
GH #1297.

Symptom: an agent opening several files in a row to show the user leaves only the LAST one visible; each open replaces the previous.

Source: openFile has no tab-vs-replace notion. UI_FILE_OPEN_MODES (shared/types/filesystem.ts:20) is only view|edit|diff — how the CONTENT renders. The command carries {path, mode?, filesystem?} (shared/ui-bridge.ts:20) and uiCommandDispatcher.ts:128 calls surface.openFile(path) on the single file surface, so consecutive opens overwrite. openPanel carries an explicit id so panels coexist; files have no equivalent identity.

Ask: multi-file representation (tabs) so opened files coexist.

Design notes: re-opening the SAME path must stay idempotent (no duplicate tabs); likely an open disposition (replace|newTab) defaulting to today's behaviour so nothing regresses; bound the tab count so a loop cannot open hundreds.

title: Gate the in-process product runtime (embedded mode) behind an explicit default-off option
description:
WHAT: The workspace server currently hot-loads external plugins' boring.server modules into the host Node process and dispatches them via /api/v1/plugins/:pluginId/* (packages/workspace/src/server/runtimeBackend/, wired in createWorkspaceAgentServer.ts around L1531/L1710/L2259). Under RECONCILIATION §13(c) this is the product runtime's 'embedded' mode and must be default-off. Add a host option productRuntime.embedded (env BORING_PRODUCT_RUNTIME_EMBEDDED=1) to createWorkspaceAgentServer; when off, do not construct/register the runtime backend gateway, make /api/v1/plugins/:pluginId/* answer 404 with a stable ErrorCode, and have reloadFromLoadedPlugins skip server modules with a per-plugin diagnostic ('embedded product runtime disabled') instead of importing them. Update packages/workspace/docs/PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md §7/§8 to describe embedded mode truthfully (today §7 lists hot server routes as a non-goal while the code serves them).

WHY: Ground truth first. P0.6 / ARCHITECTURE-PLAN D-b refuse agent-written server code in the host process; the ruling admits it only as embedded mode on single-tenant curator deployments.

File scope: packages/workspace/src/app/server/createWorkspaceAgentServer.ts; packages/workspace/src/server/runtimeBackend/*; packages/workspace/src/app/server/__tests__/runtimeBackendReload.test.ts (+ one new test file beside it); packages/workspace/docs/PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md. Do not touch agentPlugins/manager.ts front-plugin hot reload or the WorkspaceBridge.

Proof path: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace test -- runtimeBackend (existing reload test passes with the option on; new test asserts default-off → 404 + diagnostic and no dynamic import); pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace typecheck; pnpm lint:invariants.

Acceptance: default boot never imports a boring.server module from a runtime plugin; opt-in restores today's behavior unchanged; docs §7/§8 match code.

Fits one session: yes — one option, one guard, one doc section.

PRIOR WORK (360 map): docs/plans/archive/runtime-plugin-trust-modes-plan.md already defines ServerRuntime host-boot|disabled and FrontRuntime native|iframe|disabled; reuse its vocabulary for the embedded gate and cite it in the PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md note.

description:

Workspace side (DB-free): packages/workspace/src/server/productLifecycle/releases.ts exporting ProductReleaseManifest { productId; releaseDigest; parents: string[]; packageLockDigest; artifactDigests: Record<string,string>; behaviorDigest; stateCompat: {schemaVersion; migratesFrom: string[]}; provenance: {requesterId; builderRequestKey; createdAt}; evidenceRefs: string[] }, a pure computeReleaseDigest(manifest) (sha256 over canonical JSON, excluding releaseDigest), ProductReleaseStore { put(manifest) (idempotent by digest; rejects a different body under the same digest); get(digest); listByProduct(productId) }, and MemoryProductReleaseStore. Core side: drizzle migration packages/core/drizzle/0028_product_releases.sql (table product_releases: release_digest PK, product_id, workspace_id, manifest jsonb, created_at; no UPDATE path) + schema.ts entry + PostgresProductReleaseStore in packages/core/src/server/workspace/productLifecycle.ts implementing the same interface. Mirror the immutability pattern of agent_host_binding_admissions.

WHY: Without an immutable release identity nothing downstream (installation, activation, evidence) can be bound to exact behavior.

Acceptance: digest is deterministic across key order; put is idempotent; same digest + different body rejected; core store passes the shared conformance test; migration applies on a fresh DB in the core migration test.

Fits one session: yes — one record, one interface, two stores.

BINDING RULE (owner, 2026-09-07): no product record, key, or operation may reference a session id. Bind to workspaceId, installationId and threadId (nc-t Thread identity record) only; a Session is an optional runtime conversation attached to a Thread. title: Installation record + append-only activation receipts with compare-and-set
description:
Epic: https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/issues/1562 (NC-2).

WHAT: Add Installation and Activation (RECONCILIATION §13(d), §11(c) step 4). Workspace side (DB-free) in packages/workspace/src/server/productLifecycle/: ProductInstallation { installationId; workspaceId; productId; scope: 'workspace'|'personal'; ownerUserId?; runtimeMode: 'embedded'|'local'|'remote'; activeReleaseDigest: string|null; generation: number; bindings: Record<string,string>; standingPolicy: {maxChangeClass; budget}|null }, ActivationReceipt { activationId; installationId; requestKey; fromRelease; toRelease; expectedGeneration; state: 'prepared'|'committed'|'aborted'; committedAt?; reason? }, ProductInstallationStore { create; get; listByWorkspace; activate({installationId,toRelease,expectedGeneration,requestKey}) } where activate is CAS on generation (stale → {state:'aborted', reason:'stale-generation'} and no pointer move), idempotent by requestKey (replay returns the settled receipt, never a second commit), and records prepared→committed atomically. MemoryProductInstallationStore + core Postgres store with migration 0029_product_installations.sql (tables product_installations, product_activations with UNIQUE(installation_id, request_key)); use a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the installation row. Mirror agent_host_destructive_publication_events' two-phase shape.

WHY: Activation is the one write that must be durable, scoped and retry-safe; everything else is projection.

File scope: packages/workspace/src/server/productLifecycle/{installations.ts,activation.ts,memoryStore.ts,index.ts,__tests__/activation.test.ts}; packages/core/drizzle/0029_product_installations.sql; packages/core/src/server/db/schema.ts; packages/core/src/server/workspace/productLifecycle.ts. title: ProductRuntimeHost seam + embedded adapter + conformance suite
description:
Epic: https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/issues/1562 (NC-4a).

WHAT: Define the product runtime contract from RECONCILIATION §13(b)/(c) in packages/workspace/src/server/productRuntime/types.ts: ProductRuntimeHost { mode: 'embedded'|'local'|'remote'; start(installation, release, materialized: {serverEntry?: string; declaredOperations: DeclaredOperation[]}): Promise<ProductRuntimeHandle>; dispatch(handle, op, input, ctx: {workspaceId; installationId; actorId; requestKey}): Promise<unknown>; stop(handle); status(handle) } with DeclaredOperation { name; inputSchema; outputSchema; effect: 'observe'|'propose'|'mutate'|'external-effect'; capabilities: string[] }. Provide a reusable conformance suite (productRuntimeConformance(createHost)) asserting: unknown op rejected; workspace/installation mismatch rejected; stop makes dispatch fail; restart from the same release re-serves the same ops; dispatch never receives host secrets/env. Implement EmbeddedProductRuntime wrapping RuntimeBackendRegistry (only constructible when the NC-0 option is on) and run the suite against it. Register a started runtime's declared operations as brokered bridge ops product.op.<installationId>.<name> under the installation's capabilities (host-side wrapper, reuses NC-3 authorization).

WHY: The seam is what makes 'mode is policy, not code' true; local/remote adapters plug in without touching the bridge.

File scope: packages/workspace/src/server/productRuntime/{types.ts,embedded.ts,brokeredOps.ts,index.ts,__tests__/conformance.ts,__tests__/embedded.test.ts}; packages/workspace/src/server/index.ts (export). No sandbox package changes (that is NC-4b).

Proof path: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace test -- productRuntime; typecheck; pnpm lint:invariants.

Acceptance: conformance suite green for embedded; brokered op dispatch denied without capability; declared ops appear in bridge listing only while the runtime is started.

Fits one session: yes — one interface, one adapter, one suite.

PRIOR WORK (360 map): DeclaredOperation must be nc-x's Capability declaration, not a parallel contract. Check bead wt-391-forward-oueu (PiPlatform seam) and decide in the PR whether ProductRuntimeHost sits on it or beside it; cite docs/plans/agent-runtime/fleet-and-environments (Environment lease vocabulary) and docs/plans/agent-runtime/consumption-modes (a different 'modes' taxonomy — disambiguate).

title: LocalSandboxProductRuntime: serve a release's operations from a bwrap/runsc lease
description:
Epic: https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/issues/1562 (NC-4b).

WHAT: Implement ProductRuntimeHost mode 'local' in packages/workspace/src/server/productRuntime/local.ts using SandboxProviderV1 from packages/boring-sandbox (bwrap first, runsc when available): on start, provision a lease, materialize the release's server bundle (artifact digest-verified) into the lease, launch a minimal runtime process (packages/workspace/src/server/productRuntime/runtimeEntry.ts, plain Node, no host imports) that speaks a line-delimited JSON dispatch protocol over the lease's exec stdio, and proxy dispatch with per-call timeout and the ctx from NC-4a; stop disposes the lease; status reports lease health. The runtime process receives only the release artifacts and the declared operation table — no host env, no DB URL, no tokens. Run the NC-4a conformance suite against it (skip when no sandbox provider is available, exactly like existing boring-sandbox tests).

Acceptance: conformance green in local mode; killing the lease mid-dispatch yields a typed runtime-unavailable error and a fresh start re-serves; the runtime process cannot read host process.env (asserted by an op that tries).

title: First journey acceptance: live Seneca mathematics tutor installed for a second authorized learner
description:

WHAT: The epic done-bar (DIRECTION amendment 2026-09-07). First, in apps/workspace-playground, run a deterministic supporting fixture: a math-tutor product with one generated front component (exercise card) and one generated operation grade_step (deterministic checker), created through the product-builder seat (NC-6), released (NC-1), installed for a second fixture user in runtimeMode 'local' (NC-2/NC-3/NC-4b), and rendered isolated (NC-5). Write a redacted, evidence-derived live receipt to docs/issues/1562/first-journey-live-seneca-<sha>.md. Fixture-only evidence cannot close this bead or epic.

WHY: Missing proof is not a pass; this bead is the only thing that can close the epic, and it can do so only after the live Seneca acceptance required by RECONCILIATION §13(g) and LIFECYCLE E1b.

File scope: apps/workspace-playground/{fixtures/products/math-tutor/**, scripts/first-journey-acceptance.mjs, e2e/}; docs/issues/1562/. The playground fixture is deterministic support, not a substitute for the live tenant-side acceptance. No package changes — if one is needed, open a bounded bead instead.

title: Reconciliation: compatibility check, precise conflict, digest quarantine, explicit undo
description:
Epic: https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/issues/1562 (nc-r). Gap from the 360 map: the last journey stage had zero coverage.

WHAT: In packages/workspace/src/server/productLifecycle/reconcile.ts: checkCompatibility(installation, candidateRelease) → { ok } | { conflicts: Array<{ kind: schema|operation|binding|dependency; path; base; local; incoming }> } using the manifests' stateCompat, declared operations and bindings and the installation's retained local changes (a retained change = a release whose parents include the installation's base); a three-way summary (old base / local / new base) with precise, addressable conflicts; product.v1.activate refuses an incompatible release with the conflict list; product.v1.undo as an explicit bridge op = activation to the prior committed receipt's release (nc-2 primitive, surfaced); product.v1.quarantine {releaseDigest}: marks the digest quarantined, stops the product runtime serving it (nc-4a stop), blocks activation and resume, exposes recovery status. Records are appended, never rewritten.

WHY: 'A private choice survives a compatible upstream update; a real incompatibility produces a precise conflict' is the stage that makes creation maintainable.

Proof path: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace test -- reconcile.

Acceptance: compatible upstream update over a retained change activates; a schema-breaking base yields one precise conflict and no pointer move; quarantine stops dispatch within one call; undo restores prior release without touching product records.

Fits one session: yes.

title: Thread identity record: durable job root with session bindings (no timeline shape decision)
